questions.q: What does an org shape capture?
options: A source org's actual record data only
A source org's features, settings, licenses, and limits — not its data or metadata content
A full backup of a production org's Apex code
A scratch org's expiration date
questions.explain: An org shape captures the configuration profile of an org — its features, settings, licenses, and limits — deliberately without capturing any actual data or metadata content.

questions.q: What does an org snapshot capture that an org shape does not?
options: Nothing — they capture exactly the same thing
Only the scratch org's alias name
A scratch org's metadata AND data together, as a reusable point-in-time copy
Only the Dev Hub's configuration, not the scratch org's
questions.explain: Unlike an org shape (configuration only), an org snapshot captures a scratch org's metadata and data together, letting a new scratch org start already populated instead of starting empty.

questions.q: In a scratch org definition file built to match an org shape, which property replaces `edition`, and what value does it take?
options: sourceOrg, set to the source org's 15-character org ID
snapshot, set to a snapshot name
namespace, set to the registered namespace
adminEmail, set to the shape's admin user email
questions.explain: Building a scratch org from an org shape uses the sourceOrg property, set to the 15-character (not 18-character) org ID of the source org, in place of specifying edition.

questions.q: What two restrictions apply to a scratch org being used as the source for creating a new org snapshot?
options: It must be at least 30 days old and must have zero custom objects
It must already be deleted before the snapshot can be taken
It must be the Dev Hub's default org
It can't itself have been created from a snapshot, and it can't have been created with a namespace
questions.explain: A scratch org can only be used to create a new snapshot if it wasn't itself created from a snapshot and wasn't created with a namespace.

questions.q: Which feature should a team use if their problem is specifically "creating a correctly set-up scratch org takes 20 minutes every time because of a long data-seeding script"?
options: An org shape
An org snapshot
A namespace
A managed package
questions.explain: An org snapshot is the right fit when the problem is repeated, slow setup work — it captures a scratch org's metadata and data as a reusable starting point, skipping the setup entirely on future scratch org creations.
